Question Choices: A 20 N force acts north and a 12 N force acts south. What is the resultant force in newtons north?
Solution: Choose a positive axis, attach signs to collinear forces, and add the signed values. The resultant magnitude is the absolute value of the sum; a zero resultant has no direction. 20+(-12)=8 N north.

Question Choices: A plane flies 5 km/h east relative to the air while the air moves 12 km/h north relative to the ground. Find the plane's resultant ground speed in km/h.
Solution: Use a common coordinate frame. Add an object's velocity relative to the medium to the medium's velocity relative to the ground. For consecutive path legs, add displacements componentwise; straight-line displacement magnitude uses Pythagoras, while distance traveled adds the lengths of the legs. Ground velocity=(5,12); sqrt(25+144)=13 km/h.

Solution: Use a common coordinate frame. Add an object's velocity relative to the medium to the medium's velocity relative to the ground. For consecutive path legs, add displacements componentwise; straight-line displacement magnitude uses Pythagoras, while distance traveled adds the lengths of the legs. Displacement=(6,8) km; sqrt(36+64)=10 km.

Question Choices: Two forces of 7 N and 7 N act in the same direction. What is the resultant force in newtons?
Solution: Choose a positive axis, attach signs to collinear forces, and add the signed values. The resultant magnitude is the absolute value of the sum; a zero resultant has no direction. 7+7=14 N along the shared direction.

Question Choices: For the velocity (1, 1), find its direction north of east in degrees.
Solution: For a nonzero vector, measure direction counterclockwise from positive x in [0,360) degrees. Use both component signs to choose the quadrant; arctan(y/x) alone cannot distinguish opposite quadrants and is undefined when x=0. Axis directions can be read directly. Use atan2(1,1) and the component signs: theta=45 degrees in [0,360).
